items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: I played with all of these groups at that point... you've got guys like... Bobby Charles... You deal with them in groups

ctx.x: I'm going to quote this to one person, when we started to define R&B, and I think there's another element that we touched on earlier, and a friend of yours, Jerry Marksler, who was president, vice president of Atlantic Records, who produced a number of R&B records in the 50s. One said that maybe it shouldn't have been called R&B, maybe it should have been called Rhythm and Gospel, instead of Rhythm and Blues. What do you think?

I think it probably would have took on a bad thing, because the Gospel, the people in the Gospel thing, was a problem, it was like they were priming on Great Charles, and a lot of things that, you know, on the borderline of some sense of the Gospel.
I think what he meant is that there was so much Gospel influence in people.
